Each series' in-sample naive-forecast error, the scale of MASE and RMSSE

Source: R/ilm_scores.R, R/zzz-iml-aliases.R
ilm_naive_scale.Rd

The mean absolute and mean squared error of the naive forecast (the value period steps back) over each series' history: the scale that makes MASE and RMSSE comparable across series. These are the denominators of fpp3's scaled errors, the mean over t = period + 1 to T of |y_t - y_(t - period)| and of its square (section 5.8, "Scaled errors"), which fpp3 credits to Hyndman and Koehler (2006). Compute it from the data the model was trained on, and pass it to ilm_scores.ilm_pred() as naive.

Usage

ilm_naive_scale(history, time, group = NULL, response, period = 1L)

Arguments

history

A data frame: the observed history, as the model was trained on it.

time

The name of its time column.

group

The name of the column identifying each series, or NULL for a single series. The prediction's rows need the same column.

response

The name of the outcome column.

period

The lag of the naive forecast: 1 for the naive forecast, the season's length for the seasonal naive.

Value

A data frame with one row per series: key, and the naive error's mean absolute value abs and mean square sq.

Giving MASE and RMSSE their scale

The scaled errors (mase, rmsse) divide each row's error by its series' in-sample naive-forecast error, so they need each series' history. There are two ways to give it, and they give identical scores wherever both apply:

  • history = train, the common case: the data the model was trained on. The prediction already knows its time, series and response columns (it records them), so nothing else is needed. period sets the naive forecast's lag: 1, or the season's length for the seasonal naive.

  • naive = ilm_naive_scale(train, time =, group =, response =): the scale computed once and passed in. Use it when the prediction doesn't know its time column (see Time and series columns in ilm_predict()), or when several models' predictions must share one scale, so their scaled errors compare on the same footing.

When history = can't work, because the prediction has no time column, the error says so and gives the naive = call to use instead. Give one of the two, not both.

References

Hyndman, R. J. and Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition. OTexts. Section 5.8, "Evaluating point forecast accuracy" (online edition, https://otexts.com/fpp3/toolbox.html#sec-accuracy, read 27 October 2026).

Hyndman, R. J. and Koehler, A. B. (2006). Another look at measures of forecast accuracy. International Journal of Forecasting 22, 679-688.

See also

ilm_scores.ilm_pred(), which uses it for mase and rmsse.

Examples

d <- data.frame(id = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 5), t = rep(1:5, 2),
                y = c(1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 10, 12, 11, 15, 14))
ilm_naive_scale(d, time = "t", group = "id", response = "y")
#>   key  abs   sq
#> 1   a 1.75 3.75
#> 2   b 2.00 5.50
